answer.justification: The inferior thyroid artery is closely related to the recurrent laryngeal nerve near the thyroid pole. Ligating it close to the pole risks RLN injury, causing vocal cord paralysis and hoarseness. External laryngeal nerve is near superior thyroid artery; internal laryngeal nerve injury does not cause hoarseness; laryngeal edema would present earlier. Thus RLN injury is most likely.

decision.reason: Inferior thyroid artery ligated near poles risks recurrent laryngeal nerve injury. Hoarseness suggests nerve palsy. Standard anatomy; PubMed not needed.
